reference.source: Kanski's Clinical Ophthalmology / corneal dystrophy literature
clinicalPearls: A rare autosomal recessive dystrophy of subepithelial corneal amyloid deposition, linked to TACSTD2 (M1S1) mutations
It is more common in populations of Japanese descent
Presents in the first two decades with severe photophobia, watering, foreign-body sensation and progressive visual loss
The cornea develops mulberry-like gelatinous subepithelial nodules of amyloid
It is a corneal (localised) amyloidosis without systemic amyloid involvement
It recurs readily after superficial keratectomy or grafting, often necessitating repeated intervention
reference.pathophysiology: Gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy results from mutations in the TACSTD2 gene, which disrupt tight-junction-related epithelial barrier function. The resulting increased epithelial permeability is thought to allow accumulation of amyloid beneath and within the epithelium, forming the characteristic gelatinous, mulberry-like subepithelial deposits. These deposits scatter light and progressively impair vision, and because the underlying epithelial defect persists, amyloid re-accumulates rapidly after removal, explaining the high recurrence rate.
additionalDifferentials: Lattice corneal dystrophy (also amyloid, but stromal)
additionalInvestigations: Slit-lamp examination of the gelatinous subepithelial nodules
Histology or staining demonstrating amyloid where needed
Assessment of visual impact and recurrence after treatment
Confirmation that amyloidosis is localised to the cornea
reference.prognosis: The dystrophy is visually disabling and characteristically recurs after treatment, so many patients require repeated procedures; specialised ocular surface and graft strategies aim to delay recurrence.
pitfalls: Confusing it with lattice dystrophy or non-dystrophic surface deposits
Underestimating the high recurrence rate after keratectomy or grafting
Overlooking the recessive inheritance and relevant ancestry
Assuming systemic amyloidosis, which is not part of this condition
